tossups.text: After being mortally wounded by this man, Connla revealed himself as his son by showing him a red-gold thumb-ring, and this man killed his foster-brother and best friend Ferdiad after three days of battle. After months of victories in individual combat, this man was wounded by Lugaid's spear, after which he tied himself to a rock to keep his opponents from knowing he was hurt. This hero wielded the Gae Bulg, a forty-nine barbed spear, against enemies sent by Mebd to steal the bull Donn Cuailnge. For 10 points, name this Ulsterian hero of The Cattle Raid of Cooley.

In a painting by Tintoretto, this figure wears a pink robe and leans over underneath ghostly cherubs swirling around hanging lamps. In a "White" painting by Marc Chagall, this figure hangs under the script I·N·R·I. In Michelangelo's sculpture ofPieta, thisfigure is cradled in the arms of Mary. For ten points, name this religious figure who has been painted speaking to his disciples in paintings ofThe Last Supperanddying inWhite Crucifixion.

Combustion reactions produce carbon dioxide, energy, and this substance. Sometimes called the "universal solvent", it has high surface tension because it forms many hydrogen bonds. This compound is unusual in that as it is cooled, it becomes less dense, so its solid form floats on top of its liquid form. For 10 points, name this compound that boils at 100 degrees Celsius, freezes at zero degrees Celsius, and has formula H2O.

One of these devices may be formed from nickel cobaltite deposited on a carbon aerogel or onto solid activated carbon in the EDLC component of a supercapacitor. Two large and one small of these devices are used in a Trigatron spark gap switch. Doping these devices with radioactive caesium or nickel may be used to improve their switching times. In one technique, a platinum wire-based one of these devices is submerged in a solution of one Molar acid. That "standard hydrogen" example of these devices typically serves as their "reference" type in a setup involving three of them. A glass-based one of these devices is used in most lab pH meters. For 10 points, name these electrochemical cells where reduction and oxidation reactions occur.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for synaptic transmission. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this axon-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The axon is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in synaptic transmission.

tossups.text: An increased presence of this compound in the blood results in cells increasing their production of nitric oxide by binding to muscarinic receptors, which leads to vasodilation. Nerve agents like sarin prevent the production of the enzyme that breaks down this compound to its metabolites. The binding of this compound to postsynaptic receptors causes ion channels to open and allows sodium ions to flow into muscle cells, which generates an action potential that induces muscle contraction. Otto Loewi discovered this compound during an experiment where he took fluid from one heart and applied it to another. For 10 points, name this neurotransmitter derived from acetyl-CoA abbreviated AcH.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for blood types and rh factor. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this erythrocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The erythrocyte is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in blood types and rh factor.

tossups.text: The woodcarvings of the Bagaya Monastery are on the banks of this river in the former royal capital of Amarapura. Teak logs are often transported along this river, the longest in a country that supplies half of the world's teak supply. The confluence of the Mali and N'mai Rivers into this river was the planned site for the controversial Myitsone Dam. One can find George Orwell's former red brick house along the banks of this river. The Kachin people reside on the banks of this river, whose basin was the site of the Kingdom of Pagan. In one poem, Rudyard Kipling gave this river the nickname "The Road to Mandalay." For 10 points, name this longest river in Myanmar that flows into the Andaman Sea.

A funeral oration in support of this cause ends by calling its enemies "the fools, the fools, the fools!" before saying that the opposite situation "shall never be at peace." Thomas Henry Burke and Frederick Cavendish were murdered in Phoenix Park by advocates of this cause known as the "Invincibles." Following the failure of Charles Stewart Parnell's more moderate Home Rule movement, the more radical Sinn Féin ["shin-FAYN"] group arose supporting this cause. The Easter Rising was a movement in favor of, for 10 points, what effort to create a sovereign country with a capital at Dublin?

The creator of this artwork gave no instructions on how it was to be displayed; its current museum decided to use chronological order by when each of its subjects was introduced. It consists of thirty-two separate panels, mostly red on top, and mostly white on the bottom. In describing this work, the artist said "I used to have the same lunch every day, for twenty years, I guess, the same thing over and over again." For 10 points, identify this series of silkscreens by Andy Warhol depicting the containers of a certain food company's products that comes in varieties such as cream of mushroom and tomato.

this structure is essential for allergies and hypersensitivity. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this vaccine-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The vaccine is a key component of the Immune system, involved in allergies and hypersensitivity.

tossups.text: One composer from this country emphasized dissonance with quarter tones through "hypertonality" in his Threnody to the Victims of Hiroshima. A soprano sings a lament to Mary in the Symphony of Sorrowful Songs from this country. Tchaikovsky's 3rd Symphony is nicknamed after this nation, and Tchaikovsky also included this country's folk dances, like the mazurka, in his work. A composer from this nation wrote solo piano works dubbed "Torrent", "Black Keys" and "Revolutionary"; those are his 27 etudes. For 10 points, name this country home to Penderecki, Górecki and Chopin, the setting of Arnold Schoenberg's A Survivor from Warsaw.

A standard textbook used to teach this practice was written by George Belch. A "life cycle" model of this practice divides its effectiveness into introduction, growth, maturity and decline phases. The first section of a 1999 book by Naomi Klein argues that companies have been successful in implementing this practice in schools. The success of this component of the "promotional mix" can be quantified by the AIDA and DAGMAR models. Utility companies printing brochures on saving energy is an example of the "institutional" type of this practice. This practice may use sex appeal to aid in brand recall for consumers. For 10 points, name this component of marketing that uses a non-personal message to promote a product, service or idea.
acceptableAnswers: accept Advertising and Promotion as that is the title of the text referenced in the first line

tossups.text: This people were raided by people from "Ahhiyawa," which is possibly a transliteration of "Achaeans." This people called their language Neshili, meaning "the language of Nesha." This people ruled over the Hurrians, whose Mitanni Empire they conquered under the king Suppilu·liuma I. They signed the earliest surviving peace treaty after their king Hattusili II led several thousand chariots against Ramses II at the Battle of Kadesh. They seem to have been the first people to produce iron tools. Hattusa was the capital of-for 10 points-what people that ruled Anatolia throughout the second millenium B.C.?

This god's son Picus was too young to succeed him as a king, and this god was identified as "the sower" with the name Consivius. With the nymph Camasene, he fathered a son who drowned in the Albula River, causing it to be renamed. The father of Tiberinus, this god sprung hot water geysers in the faces of the attacking Sabines, and his temple was closed in times of peace. For 10 points, name this Roman god of beginnings, ends, and doorways who notably has two faces and is the namesake of the first month.

The quandary of whether one could square this shape with a compass and straightedge was proven impossible in 1882. A conic section becomes this shape when the eccentricity drops to zero. The polar equation "r equals one" graphs this shape, as does the standard equation "x squared plus y squared equals one". This shape can be determined uniquely by its center and radius. For 10 points, name this shape whose area formula is pi times the radius squared.

Guillem de Torroella claimed to have been kidnapped and taken to this place in order to entertain its immortal king, and in some versions of his story, Ogier the Dane eventually reaches this place and marries its former ruler. According to some sources, this place is ruled by nine sisters, including Glitonea, Thiten, and Morgan. This place is also known as 'The Fortunate Isle', as crops grow without being cultivated, including the apple trees from which this island takes its name. One notable inhabitant of this place travelled there in a black boat following the Battle of Camlann, and will return one day to lead his people against their enemies. For 10 points, name this mystical island in British mythology, the resting place of King Arthur.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for cranial nerves. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cranial nerve-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cranial nerve is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in cranial nerves.

tossups.text: Jonathan Lambert, a whaler from this city, colonized Tristan da Cunha ("COON-yuh") as the "Islands of Refreshment." This city's East India Marine Society sold "amerikani" cloth to Zanzibar and imported pepper on the Friendship, whose attack incited the First Sumatran expedition. This city and Lawrence were the seats of the gerrymandered Essex County. This city was divided into an isolated rural "Village," now called Danvers, which was dominated by the feuding Porters and Putnams, and an urban "Town" whose port was inspected by the native Nathaniel Hawthorne. In this city, Samuel Parris enslaved a Carib woman who, like Sarah Good, was blamed with "spectral evidence" for making Betty Parris and Abigail Williams suffer fits. For 10 points, Tituba was accused of serving Satan in what city's 1692 witch trials?

This character reads a horoscope that tells him his life will be changed by a red bull in a field of green, which comes to pass when he sees the flag of a military unit called the Mavericks. He wears a locket opened by the chaplain Arthur Bennett, which contains a note from his father and a baptism certificate. He saves the life of the horse trader Mahbub Ali and becomes the disciple of a lama who is searching for the River of the Arrow. That lama pays for his education at St. Xavier's before he steals valuable papers from some French and Russian spies. Although his mother is Irish, his skin becomes dark under the sun of Lahore. For 10 points, name this orphan who aids the British secret service as the title character of a novel by Rudyard Kipling.

parts.text: This god replaced his cupbearer Hebe with Ganymede, whom he had abducted in the form of an eagle.
This goddess of dawn ended up with a cicada for a husband after granting Tithonus of Troy immortality but forgetting to also give him eternal youth.
After killing her husband Priam and son Astyanax, this Greek kidnapped Andromache, though that was more as a spoil of war than as a lover. This man was also known as Pyrrhus.

bonuses.leadin: Poor Trojans! The gods keep on kidnapping them for lovers. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Italian artist, who also designed the dome of St. Peter's Basilica. He may be better known for his frescos on the Sistine Chapel.
One of Michelangelo's most famous sculptures is this depiction of Mary holding the body of Jesus after the crucifixion.
Due to a mistranslation, Michelangelo's statue of this biblical character was depicted with horns.

bonuses.leadin: This sculptor created works for the Tomb of Pope Julius II, which did not include his Dying Slave and Rebellious Slave. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this transition value where liquid becomes a vapor. For pure water at atmospheric pressure, the temperature for this value is 100 degrees Celsius.
Boiling point and vapor pressure are examples of this type of property, which depends on the ratio of solute to solvent and not on the properties of the chemicals themselves.

The number of particles used to calculate changes due to colligative properties is named after this Dutch scientist. His namesake factor, symbolized lowercase i, notes how ionic compounds dissociate in solution.

bonuses.leadin: This value increases when a solute is added to a solvent. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name these protein shells that enclose the genetic material in viruses. Adenoviruses use 252 identical proteins to make up its polyhedral version of this structure.
Many of the most common capsids are found in this type of virus, named for the type of organisms they infect. These tailed viruses include the T4 which infects E. Coli
This type of virus features an envelope with glycoprotein spikes that protects its eight helical capsids. Doctors recommend getting a yearly vaccine for this virus in its namesake "season".

bonuses.leadin: These structures may be rod-shaped, polyhedral, or near spherical. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with hepatic portal system.
What is the main function of the liver in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to hepatic portal system.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Identify this problem of graph theory which can be solved using Dijkstra's Algorithm.
Like the Shortest Path Tree Problem, this problem seeks to optimize the selection of edges to link all nodes and yields the namesake structure with the lowest possible edge weight.
The Minimal Spanning Tree Problem can be solved using Prim's Algorithm or this other algorithm, which selects subsequent edges that do not form a circuit with existing edges.

bonuses.leadin: For an undirected graph containing nodes and edges with an associated length, a root node is identified and routes to each node from the root are found such that the paths are minimized. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with bone structure and types.
What is the main function of the skull in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to bone structure and types.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: What state's place names include Lake Char·gogg·a·gogg·man·chau·gga·gogg·chau·bu·na·gung·a·maugg, as well as the England-inspired Charles River and university-dense city of Cambridge?

The Wachusett Reservoir also feeding Boston is near this city in central Massachusetts. This city, whose name has two syllables, was named for an English city home to the condiment maker Lea & Perrins.

This town on the Massachusetts North Shore home to a Singing Beach is also named for an English place, but added a location-based phrase to its name in 1989 to disambiguate from a larger city in nearby New Hampshire.

bonuses.leadin: This state's largest body of water, the Quabbin Reservoir, feeds its largest city and means "meeting of the waters" in Nipmuc. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these three-tiered, two-masted Greek ships that were captained by trierarchs and held epibatai, or marines. They could maneuver easily and quickly ram enemy ships, but carried few soldiers.
This class of large rowing ships included triremes, penteconters, and many others.
This empire used the somewhat outdated Phoenician navy in its two invasions of Greece, but it was defeated at Salamis and Mycale.

bonuses.leadin: A silver strike at the Laurium deposit resulted in the construction of 100 of these ships by Athens, although they were invented by the Phoenicians. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this term defined as the speed of music. This concept can be measured in beats per minute and is described by Italian terms such as adagio and presto.
This Italian word, translated as "cheerful," describes tempos faster than moderato and slower than presto.
Music in a faster tempo often substitutes common time with this other time signature, written as a C with a slash through it.

bonuses.leadin: Metronomes are tools used to set and maintain this concept in music. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with synaptic transmission.
What is the main function of the axon in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to synaptic transmission.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: This Roman temple features a concrete dome with hollow coffers, a checkerboard floor pattern, and a large circular oculus.
Arches and tunnels maintain the constant slant required for the smooth flow of water through these structures.
The Arch of Titus near the Roman Forum depicts Titus' successful sacking and looting of this city.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about ancient Roman architecture, for 10 points each:

parts.text: What founder of academic anthropology in the US was disappointed by what he saw as the unwillingness of Americans to enter into creative empathy with those Kwakiutl people?

Boas attacked racist notions of intellectual capability in this 1911 magnum opus, arguing that so-called "uncivilized" people had different frameworks for knowledge rather than being intellectually inferior.
Boas started the first academic department of anthropology at this Ivy League university.

bonuses.leadin: This academic set up a living diorama of Kwakiutl life at the 1893 World Columbian Exposition. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this conflict that began in 1983 and was fought between a group led by Velupillai Prabhakaran (VEL-oo-pil-ai preb-AH-kuh-run) and a government dominated by the Sinhalese (SIN-uh-leez) ethnicity.
This ethnic group's "Liberation Tigers" fought against the Sinhalese government in Sri Lanka until its surrender in 2009.
The Tamil Tigers assassinated Rajiv, an Indian prime minister with this surname. Rajiv was the son of Indira, another assassinated Indian prime minister with this surname.

bonuses.leadin: During this conflict, a group fought to establish an ethnic homeland, in a territory the organization called "Eelam" (EE-lahm). For 10 points each:

parts.text: After insulting the Aesir and fleeing into a waterfall, Loki was caught by this deity. This Norse god of thunder wields the hammer Mjolnir.
After Loki lost a bet, one of these beings named Brokkr sewed Loki's lips shut after being forbidden from touching his neck. Another one of these beings named Eitri created Gungnir and Mjolnir.

After Loki was bound to a rock, this jotunn fasted a venomous snake above him to drip poison on him for eternity. This figure married Njord after choosing her husband based solely on looking at their feet.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Loki being punished for his hijinks, for ten points each:

parts.text: Name these meteorological events which are "hunted" by WC-130 pilots, who fly in and out of their eyewall while collecting pressure and wind speed data.

This US governmental agency, which operates the National Weather Service and National Ocean Service, employs a team of hurricane hunters to gather data for forecasting. In 2019, officials in this agency were threatened if they didn't support Donald Trump's mistaken claim that Hurricane Dorian would hit Alabama.
acceptableAnswers: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration

parts.text: Hurricanes are classified on the Saffir-Simpson scale, which uses this classification for the most severe storms. A hurricane must have sustained winds of at least one hundred fifty-seven miles per hour to reach this status.

bonuses.leadin: The WC-130 is a Lockheed airplane modified for collecting data from these events. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this agricultural tool used to separate grain which became a symbol of pharaonic power.
The flail and crook were originally symbols of this Egyptian god, the husband of Isis.
Another royal symbol in Egypt was the uraeus ("yoo-RAY-us"), one of these animals. One of these animals is found beside a vulture on the forehead of the golden mask of Tutankhamun.

bonuses.leadin: Tutankhamun holds a crook and this other object on his coffinette. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with layers of the heart wall.
What is the main function of the atrium in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to layers of the heart wall.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Crazy Horse was a war leader for the Oglála band of this Native American people, a subgroup of the Sioux.

Crazy Horse fought alongside a chief of the Oglála Lakota during this chief's namesake war. Jealous of Crazy Horse's reputation, this leader would later start rumors that eventually led to the death of Crazy Horse.
The incomplete Crazy Horse Memorial was carved out of a mountainside in South Dakota's Black Hills, like this Gutzon Borglum sculpture featuring the faces of four presidents.

bonuses.leadin: Despite his reserved personality, Crazy Horse is remembered as a brave warrior who fiercely resisted the spread of American settler colonialism. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this 15th century French poet, whose "Ballad of the Hanged Ladies" includes the line "Where are the snows of yesteryear?"

"The Ballad of the Hanged Ladies" appears in this long poem by Villon. Based on the earlier poem The Legacy, this highly digressive poem is presented as the work of an old, dying man reflecting on his misspent youth.

This contemporary of Villon wrote poems such as "While Looking Towards the Country of France" about his exile in England. This nobleman was imprisoned for twenty-five years after being captured at the Battle of Agincourt.

bonuses.leadin: This author was arrested after killing the priest Philippe Sarmoise. For 10 points each:
